language.note: Alemannic Swiss-German dialect spoken locally; standard German used in writing

terrainDescription.zh: 地形以阿爾卑斯山地為主，西側萊茵河谷提供狹窄的農業平原，是全球少數的雙重內陸國之一（鄰國瑞士也是內陸國）。
terrainDescription.en: Predominantly Alpine terrain, with a narrow agricultural strip along the Rhine valley in the west; one of the world's few "doubly landlocked" countries (its neighbor Switzerland is landlocked too).

plate.color: white characters on a black background (distinct from Switzerland/Austria's white-background plates)
plate.shape: front 300×80mm, rear 500×110mm; format FL 12345 ("FL" + small Liechtenstein coat of arms + up to 5 digits)

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Not independently documented; the country closely follows Swiss legislation and infrastructure, so likely resembles Switzerland's black-and-white curved bollards — treat as an inference, not a confirmed fact

utilityPole.transformerMount: Not independently documented; inferred similarity to Switzerland/Austria's common round wooden poles given shared Alpine infrastructure norms — low confidence

historicalContext.zh: 列支敦士登為德語系阿爾卑斯微型國家，2020年才正式加入維也納道路標誌公約，法規與基礎建設高度承襲鄰國瑞士（甚至使用瑞士法郎作為貨幣）。
historicalContext.en: Liechtenstein is a German-speaking Alpine microstate that only formally joined the Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals in 2020; its regulations and infrastructure closely follow neighboring Switzerland's (it even uses the Swiss franc as currency).
